questiontext.text:
You are watching a boat at sea from an observation point, \(O\).

From your location the boat, at point \(B\), is on a bearing of \({@obsBoatAng@}^\circ\).
You can also see a lighthouse, at point \(L\), on a bearing of \({@obsLightAng@}^\circ\).
From the boat, the lighthouse is on a bearing of \({@boatLightAng@}^\circ\).

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="500px"]] var obsBoatAng = {#obsBoatAng#}; var obsLightAng = {#obsLightAng#}; var boatLightAng = {#boatLightAng#}; var obsLightDist = {#obsLightDist#}; JXG.Options.text.useMathJax=true; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingBox:[-13.8,5.5,16.2,-24.5], showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:true }); // Points var pointStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, showInfoBox:false, withLabel:true, name:" ", label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, fontSize:20, offset:[0,0], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; pointStyle.name = "\\(O\\)"; pointStyle.label.offset = [-30,5]; var obsPoint = board.create("point", [0,0], pointStyle); pointStyle.name = "\\(L\\)"; var lightPoint = board.create("point", [-9.2,-7.7], pointStyle); pointStyle.name = "\\(B\\)"; pointStyle.label.offset = [15,5]; var boatPoint = board.create("point", [11.3,-19.5], pointStyle); // Joining points with lines var lineStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, dash:1, name:"", withLabel:true, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, fontSize:15, offset:[0,0], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; board.create("segment", [lightPoint, boatPoint], lineStyle); lineStyle.name = "\\(".concat(obsLightDist,"km\\)"); lineStyle.label.offset = [-40,20]; board.create("segment", [obsPoint, lightPoint], lineStyle); lineStyle.name = "\\(x\\)"; lineStyle.label.offset = [5,20]; board.create("segment", [obsPoint, boatPoint], lineStyle); // Adding in north arrows var arrowStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black", name:"\\(N\\)", withLabel:true, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, fontSize:10, offset:[-5,60], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; var obsNorthPoint = board.create("point", [0,3], {visible:false}); var boatNorthPoint = board.create("point", [11.3,-16.5], {visible:false}); var lightNorthPoint = board.create("point", [-9.2,-4.7], {visible:false}); board.create("arrow", [obsPoint, obsNorthPoint], arrowStyle); board.create("arrow", [boatPoint, boatNorthPoint], arrowStyle); board.create("arrow", [lightPoint, lightNorthPoint], arrowStyle); // Adding angles var angleStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, name:" ", radius:1.75, withLabel:true, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black", fontSize:12, offset:[0,0], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; board.create("angle", [lightPoint, boatPoint, boatNorthPoint], angleStyle); [[/jsxgraph]]

Here is a worked solution:

To simplify the diagram, exclude the observation point:

[[jsxgraph width="280px" height="160px"]] var boatLightAng = {#boatLightAng#}; JXG.Options.text.useMathJax=true; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingBox:[-7,3,7,-5], showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:true }); // Points var pointStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, showInfoBox:false, withLabel:true, name:" ", label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, fontSize:15, offset:[-25,25], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; pointStyle.name = "\\(L\\)"; var lightPoint = board.create("point", [-3,0], pointStyle); pointStyle.name = "\\(B\\)"; var boatPoint = board.create("point", [3,-2], pointStyle); // Joining points with lines var lineStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, dash:1, name:"", withLabel:true, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, fontSize:15, offset:[0,0], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; board.create("line", [lightPoint, boatPoint], lineStyle); // Adding in north arrows var arrowStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black", name:"\\(N\\)", withLabel:true, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, fontSize:10, offset:[-5,50], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; var boatNorthPoint = board.create("point", [3,0], {visible:false}); var lightNorthPoint = board.create("point", [-3,2], {visible:false}); board.create("arrow", [boatPoint, boatNorthPoint], arrowStyle); board.create("arrow", [lightPoint, lightNorthPoint], arrowStyle); // Adding angles var angleStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, name:" ", radius:1, withLabel:true, label:{ fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black", fontSize:12, offset:[0,0], useMathJax:true, parse:false } }; angleStyle.name = "\\(".concat(boatLightAng, "^\\circ\\)"); angleStyle.label.offset = [0,-15]; board.create("angle", [lightPoint, boatPoint, boatNorthPoint], angleStyle); angleStyle.name = " "; angleStyle.fillColor = "purple"; angleStyle.strokeColor = "purple"; board.create("angle", [boatPoint, lightPoint, lightNorthPoint], angleStyle); var anglePoint = board.create("point", [-6,1], {visible:false}); angleStyle.fillColor = "red"; angleStyle.strokeColor = "red"; board.create("angle", [anglePoint, lightPoint, boatPoint], angleStyle); [[/jsxgraph]]

Due to the north lines being parallel, the sum of the purple and pink angles around \(L\) is equal to the sum of the orange angle at \(B\).

The lower pink angle is that of a straight line, so it is \(180^\circ\).
The upper purple angle is the bearing for which we are solving.

Therefore, we find the bearing of \(B\) from \(L\) as: \({@boatLightAng@} - 180 = {@tans1@}^\circ\).

You have found the angle between the lines \(OL\) and \(LB\).
However, bearings must be measured from the north-pointing line.

You have found the angle between the north-pointing line and the line \(LB\), measuring anti-clockwise around \(L\).
However, a bearing should be measured clockwise.

You have found the bearing of {@if float(ans1)=float(obsBoatAng) then "point \\(B\\) from point \\(O\\)" else if float(ans1)=float(obsLightAng) then "point \\(L\\) from point \\(O\\)" else if float(ans1)=float(obsLightAng-180) then "point \\(O\\) from point \\(L\\)" else if float(ans1)=float(boatLightAng) then "point \\(L\\) from point \\(B\\)" else if float(ans1)=float(180+obsBoatAng) then "point \\(O\\) from point \\(B\\)"@}.
However, you should have found the bearing of point \\(B\\) from point \\(L\\).

angleStyle.name = " "; angleStyle.fillColor = "red"; angleStyle.strokeColor = "red"; board.create("angle", [obsPoint, lightPoint, lightNorthPoint], angleStyle); board.create("angle", [lightPoint, obsPoint, obsSouthPoint], angleStyle); [[/jsxgraph]]

Because the north lines are parallel, the alternating red angles are equal in size.
Looking at point \(O\), the red angle is also \(180^\circ\) less than the bearing of \(L\) from \(O\), and so equals \({@obsLightAng-180@}^\circ\).

The sum of the red angle at point \(L\) and the angle \(B\hat{L}O\) is equal to the bearing of \(B\) from \(L\).
So, using part (a): \(B\hat{L}O = {@tans1@} - {@obsLightAng-180@} = {@tans2@}^\circ\).

Your answer is not the correct angle \(B\hat{L}O\).
However, it is consistent with the answer that you gave in part (a).

You have incorrectly determined the bearing of \(O\) from \(L\).
This bearing is an alternate angle to the bearing of \(L\) from \(O\) minus \(180^\deg\).
Therefore, the bearing of \(O\) from \(L\) is: \({@obsLightAng@} - 180 = {@obsLightAng-180@}^\circ\).
You have found the angle \({@if float(ans2)=float(180+obsBoatAng-boatLightAng) then "O\\hat{B}L" else if float(ans2)=float(obsLightAng-obsBoatAng) then "L\\hat{O}B"@}\).

To determine the length \(x\), we wish to use the sine rule and so first we need to find the green angle \(O\hat{B}L\).

Because the north lines are parallel, the alternating purple angles are equal in size.
Looking at point \(O\), the sum of the purple angle and bearing of \(B\) from \(O\) is also \(180^\circ\), and so the purple angle equals \({@180-obsBoatAng@}^\circ\).

Looking at \(B\), the sum of the green, purple and orange angles is \(360^\circ\) so the green angle is: \(360 - {@boatLightAng@} - {@180-obsBoatAng@} = {@180+obsBoatAng-boatLightAng@}^\circ\).

Now employing the sine rule: \(\frac{x}{sin({@tans2@})} = \frac{{@obsLightDist@}}{sin({@180+obsBoatAng-boatLightAng@})}\)

\(x = {@obsLightDist@} \times \frac{sin({@tans2@})}{sin({@180+obsBoatAng-boatLightAng@})}\)

\(x = {@float(tans3)@}\)

\(x = {@significantfigures(tans3,3)@}km\) (to 3sf)
